title: Sharded token-window rerank: reduce P95 latency and improve scale for dense candidate sets
creator: Priya Singh
description: Problem: The current rerank endpoint serializes candidate scoring which causes high P95/P99 latency when request candidate sets exceed ~32 items or include long-sequence tokens. This impacts customers that ship search and recommendations where tail latency matters. Goals: (1) reduce P95 latency by at least 25–35% across typical rerank workloads (32–256 candidates), (2) scale throughput across multiple CPU/GPU shards without regressions in quality or token cost, (3) keep end-to-end determinism for rerank sorting where possible.
proposed_solution: Introduce a sharded token-window parallelization for rerank scoring: partition candidates into N shards, issue parallel scoring RPCs to worker shards with a per-shard token budget and a short soft timeout, then merge partial results. Key pieces: (a) shard scheduler that balances by token budget and model KV cache affinity; (b) per-shard token_limit and soft_deadline (e.g., 60ms) with graceful partial scoring; (c) hedging policy to issue a fallback (lower-quality smaller model) if a shard misses deadline; (d) KV cache reuse across shards for repeated prefixes to avoid redundant work; (e) deterministic merge strategy that preserves tie-breaking and score normalization. We'll expose token_limit and soft_deadline as configurable per-tenant knobs and add conservative defaults optimized for latency-sensitive rerank use cases.
acceptance_criteria: P95 rerank latency decreases >= 25% on benchmark suite (32, 64, 128 candidate mixes) compared to baseline
End-to-end throughput scales >3x when using 4 shards for large candidate sets with <5% quality delta (NDCG@10) vs baseline
No more than 5% increase in per-token cost on average for production traffic profiles
Integration tests exercising soft_deadline, hedging, and partial scoring pass in CI
Console dashboard exposes per-shard latency, per-shard queue depth, and hedging events
Rollout can be toggled via feature-flag per-customer with automatic fallback to single-threaded path
implementation_notes: Scheduler: implement token-aware greedy bin-packing to allocate candidates to shards minimizing max token budget; initial heuristic uses candidate_token_counts precomputed during embed phase
Worker changes: extend scoring RPC to accept candidate slice + token_budget + soft_deadline; return (scores, computed_tokens, partial_ok flag)
Timeouts: soft_deadline triggers best-effort partial scoring return; hard_deadline enforced at runtime layer to avoid stuck requests
KV cache: add shard-level cache tags so adjacent shards reuse prefix cache entries instead of duplicating KV loads
Hedging: if a shard misses soft_deadline, trigger a fast lightweight scorer (quantized 4-bit model) in parallel and race to completion
Determinism: maintain original candidate ordering metadata and stable-sort by (score, original_index) during merge
Metrics: new metrics: rerank.shard.latency.pXX, rerank.shard.hedge.count, rerank.shard.partial_returns, rerank.merge.skipped_candidates
Testing: create synthetic harness with candidate sequences up to 512 items and variable token lengths; add canary with 5% production traffic before broad rollout
implementation_plan: Week 1: design doc + API surface (internal RPC extension) + load-test harness (Priya/Jonah)
Week 2: implement scheduler and worker RPC handling; add soft_deadline path (Eng pair)
Week 3: KV cache tagging + hedging path + metrics emission; integration tests
Week 4: canary rollout (5%), monitor dashboards, collect perf and quality signals
Week 5: iterate on heuristics, update defaults, broad rollout and postmortem
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: partial scoring could change ranking quality systematically. Mitigation: normalization step in merge + benchmark NDCG regression checks and conservative default thresholds
Risk: additional complexity in scheduler may add cost. Mitigation: enable per-tenant opt-in and telemetry to measure cost delta; tune token_limit to bound extra work
Risk: KV cache coherence across shards could increase memory. Mitigation: implement soft TTL and shared LRU tags to cap memory growth
Risk: hedging introduces extra model invocations on tails. Mitigation: track hedge rate and only enable hedging when soft_deadline miss probability > threshold
testing_plan: Unit tests for scheduler allocation heuristics
Component tests for worker RPCs honoring token_budget and soft_deadline
Integration tests end-to-end with rerank API mocking client and shard workers
Performance benchmark suite in k8s perf-cluster comparing baseline vs sharded implementation across representative org traffic
Canary: enable for internal staging orgs and then 5% of PROD traffic with automatic rollback if P95 increases by >10%
